title: African Youth Policy & Futures Fellowship
tagline: Training the next generation of African technocrats, policy architects, and strategic futurists.
description: A 9-month immersive fellowship connecting emerging researchers with African Union, regional economic community, and municipal policy advisors. Fellows translate field data into actionable legislative frameworks and horizon roadmaps.
eligibility: Aged 21–32 residing in or of the African diaspora committed to return
Demonstrated background in public policy, economics, law, sociology, or STEM
Evidence of prior community research, publication, or civic grassroots engagement
Commitment of 15 hours/week for synchronous sessions and fieldwork

howToParticipate.title: Online Application
howToParticipate.description: Submit CV, academic credentials, and a 500-word policy statement addressing an African socio-economic challenge.

howToParticipate.title: Futures Challenge Brief
howToParticipate.description: Shortlisted candidates complete a 48-hour diagnostic policy brief analyzing horizon trends.

howToParticipate.title: Panel Interview
howToParticipate.description: Meet with AfriYouth senior faculty and institutional partner representatives.

howToParticipate.title: Onboarding & Placement
howToParticipate.description: Commence induction in Kigali and receive assignment to an AU/national policy desk.

outcomes: 86% of alumni now advising ministries, international NGOs, or multilateral agencies across 22 African nations.

title: CivicTech & Social Enterprise Incubator
tagline: De-risking and scaling tech-enabled solutions that solve public delivery bottlenecks.
description: An intensive 6-month incubator providing early-stage African founders with seed funding, technical mentorship, HCD validation, and regulatory sandbox access across Eastern and Western Africa.
eligibility: Founding team majority aged 18–35 with African nationality
Functional MVP with verified initial user traction or pilot deployment
Focus areas: AgriTech, HealthTech, Climate Resilience, EdTech, or GovTech
At least one full-time technical or research co-founder

howToParticipate.title: Venture Dossier
howToParticipate.description: Submit pitch deck, operational metrics, demo video, and theory of change.

howToParticipate.title: Technical & Field Review
howToParticipate.description: AfriYouth venture team conducts product audit, community impact review, and code inspection.

howToParticipate.title: Pitch Day Selection
howToParticipate.description: Top 25 ventures pitch before investment committee and partner impact funds.

howToParticipate.title: Lab Deployment
howToParticipate.description: $25,000 catalytic grant disbursed with access to AfriYouth prototyping labs and legal advisors.

curriculumHighlights: Human-Centered Product Sprints for Low-Bandwidth Environments
Unit Economics & Sustainable Monetization in Frontier Markets
outcomes: $4.2M follow-on funding raised by cohort companies; 180,000+ citizens served.

title: Community HCD Action Studios
tagline: Grassroots co-design studios that bridge community lived experience directly into institutional design.
description: A 12-week design sprint pairing grassroots youth organizers with municipal planners to solve localized infrastructure, health access, and waste management challenges using empathetic design methodologies.
eligibility: Community youth advocates, informal settlement leaders, or local innovators aged 18–30
Active residency in pilot municipalities (Nairobi County, Accra Metropolitan, Kigali City)
Strong desire to master participatory research, user journey mapping, and physical rapid prototyping

howToParticipate.title: Community Nomination or Application
howToParticipate.description: Apply individually or receive nomination through local youth council or community CBO.

howToParticipate.title: Studio Workshop Audition
howToParticipate.description: Participate in a collaborative 1-day sprint addressing an active municipal challenge.

howToParticipate.title: Field Deployment
howToParticipate.description: Embedded in local ward research teams with direct stipend and prototype budget.

curriculumHighlights: Ethnographic Research in African Urban Contexts
Rapid Prototyping with Recycled & Low-Cost Materials
Transitioning Community Solutions into Sustainable Enterprise
outcomes: 34 municipal service improvements co-designed and officially adopted across 4 capital cities.

title: Grassroots Evidence-to-Policy Labs
tagline: Empowering youth researchers to gather hyper-local data and author credible policy briefs.
description: Collaborative research cohorts running real-time field surveys, crowdsourced citizen science, and policy impact assessments across agricultural, climate, and informal labor sectors.
eligibility: Young researchers, data analysts, or postgraduate scholars with statistical or qualitative proficiency
Working knowledge of R, Python, SPSS, or mobile survey tools (ODK, KoboToolbox)
Passion for public sector transparency and evidence-based governance

howToParticipate.title: Research Profile Submission
howToParticipate.description: Provide sample research writing, quantitative analysis sample, and areas of thematic interest.

howToParticipate.title: Methodology Briefing
howToParticipate.description: Align with AfriYouth Research Council standards and data ethics protocols.

howToParticipate.title: Commission Assignment
howToParticipate.description: Join an active research consortium backed by bilateral development partners.

curriculumHighlights: Digital Data Collection & Mobile Field Management
Open Data Standards and Peer Review Practices
outcomes: Over 50 policy papers cited by UNECA, African Development Bank, and national ministries.
